findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr182_cas_axes.py:5-8 (docstring claim) vs :89-93 (PASS condition ignores computed) and :125-148 (verify_envelopes never touches computed/expected); .agent-harness/scripts/cas_gate.py:169-187 (_check_axis_result fields only); tests/pr_cards/test_pr_182_...py:134-157 (mutation caught via 'different contract hash', not value comparison); live demo: mutated copy of docs/generated/pr182_cas/axis_result_sympy.json passes with errors=[]
findings.summary: The frozen contract's expected_exact_values block is enforced nowhere: the axis runner's PASS gate checks only the obligation keyset and boolean values, and verify_envelopes (--check) never compares envelope 'computed' against the contract — yet the module docstring claims '--check re-verifies envelope integrity (contract binding, source hashes, obligation keyset, expected values)'. Demonstrated live: an envelope with computed fixture_TB_flip='3/7->3/7' and n_prime_diagonal='[0, 1, 1]' (contradicting the contract) produces zero errors under the verify_envelopes logic. cas_gate.py check-axis/adjudicate also never read checks/computed content (only status vocabulary, contract hash, commands, evidence_class, completed_at). The stale-contract test only exercises HASH binding (its edit of expected_exact_values fails because the hash changed, not because values were compared), so the freeze of expected values is decorative.

findings.evidence: formal_pr182/Pr182Parity.lean:35-41 (hardcoded computed strings; also hardcoded engine_version 'lean4:v4.31.0-core' at :42); docs/generated/pr182_cas/axis_result_lean.json:20-26 (same strings sealed as 'computed'); tests/pr_cards/test_pr_182_...py:88-92 (these keys feed the cross-engine agreement set)
findings.summary: The Lean exe's 'computed' block is hand-typed string literals, not values derived from the verified terms — 'fixed_space_dim':'1', 'fixture_TB_flip':'3/7->-3/7', 'fixture_EB_flip':'-2/5->2/5', 'n_prime_diagonal':'[0, -1, -1]', and the full boost list are hardcoded in main. These constants flow verbatim into the sealed envelope's computed dict and are then counted by test_envelopes_bound_blind_and_obligation_uniform's 'cross-engine disagreement' assertion, making the Lean leg of the cross-engine agreement check vacuous (agreement with a copy-pasted expectation, not an independent computation). The boolean checks are genuine decide calls; the computed provenance is not.

findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr182_cas_axes.py:57-65 (wolfram branch returns no 'computed'); docs/generated/pr182_cas/axis_result_wolfram_xact.json:20 ("computed": {}) and :33 (PR182_COMPUTED only in transcript_tail); wolfram/pr182_parity_axis.wls:66 (key 'boost_coefficient_lists_flat')
findings.summary: The Wolfram axis's computed output is silently discarded: _parse_axis_json for wolfram_xact returns only {checks, all_pass}, so the sealed wolfram envelope has computed={} and the PR182_COMPUTED line survives only in the 1200-char transcript_tail. Consequently the cross-engine computed-agreement test skips Wolfram entirely (the 'if key in env.computed' guard), and its boost list uses a different key name ('boost_coefficient_lists_flat') that could never match anyway. The 4-way computed agreement is really sympy vs sage (with lean hand-typed per H2).

findings.evidence: wolfram/pr182_parity_axis.wls:4-5 (xactLoaded = True unconditional), :71 (PR182_XACT printed but never parsed); scripts/codex_harness/run_pr182_cas_axes.py:57-65 (no PR182_XACT check); docs/generated/pr182_cas/CAS_CONTRACT_PR182_PARITY.json:47 (obligation text); envelope transcript_tail shows xTensor loaded (factual mitigation)
findings.summary: The Wolfram axis's xAct identity receipt is unenforced: xactLoaded is set to True unconditionally after Needs (a Needs failure prints a message and continues; none of the seven checks use xAct), the script would still Exit[0] with all checks true, and the runner never inspects the PR182_XACT line — so the contract obligation 'load xAct and independently verify' can be satisfied-in-label with xAct absent. The sealed envelope happens to show xTensor 1.3.0 actually loaded, so the shipped PASS is factually fine; the enforcement gap remains.

findings.summary: Axis-name vocabulary drift between governance surfaces and the enforced contract: spec and backlog require axes [wolfram_xact, sympy_high_precision, sage_singular, lean_mathlib], but the frozen contract, cas_gate AXES, and all envelopes use (wolfram_xact, sympy, sage_singular, lean); nothing machine-checks required_axes against the contract's axes keys, and 'lean_mathlib' mislabels a lane the spec itself describes as no-mathlib Lean core (mitigated by the inline disclosure).

findings.evidence: scripts/codex_harness/run_pr182_cas_axes.py:70-79 (timeout= passed, no TimeoutExpired handler), :96-101 (rc in (124,127) only); spec pr182_spec.yaml:71 missing_axis_outcome: CAS_BLOCKED
findings.summary: Runner robustness/status-semantics gaps in _run_axis: (a) subprocess.TimeoutExpired is uncaught (spec timeouts are passed to subprocess.run), so a hung engine crashes --run mid-loop leaving a mixed-generation envelope set on disk; (b) BLOCKED_PLATFORM_OR_LICENSE is assigned only for returncodes 124/127, but a wolframscript license failure typically exits with a different nonzero code and would be sealed as FAIL, driving the terminal to CAS_FAIL/REGISTRY_WITHHELD when the contract semantics call for CAS_BLOCKED (missing/blocked axis).

findings.evidence: formal_pr182/Pr182Parity/Basic.lean:94-101 (kernelCoeff definition carries the mathematical content), :85-91 (only sqrt truncation grounded), header :1-9 discloses the split; docs/generated/pr182_cas/CAS_CONTRACT_PR182_PARITY.json:6-23 (four Lean sources, manifest absent); formal_pr182/Pr182Parity.lean:42 (hardcoded version string)
findings.summary: Lean lane weaknesses (disclosed but worth recording): the I4 check is near-definitional — kernelCoeff is DEFINED as the gamma-inverse/geometric convolution asserted in a comment, so boost_kernel_orders only reads back gammaInvCoeffs (grounded solely by the convSquareCoeff = (1-b^2) truncation identity); the mu-only-coefficients claim has no Lean representation at all. Additionally formal_pr182/lake-manifest.json is not among the contract's pinned Lean sources, and the toolchain actually used at run time is attested only by the hardcoded engine_version string, not measured.

notes: Positive verifications that PASSED: contract sha b73d39ed... matches adjudication and all four envelope bindings; spec sha 2dba7169... matches contract pin and card; freeze-before-seal chronology holds (contract committed 517ad952 at 2026-07-20T14:42:21Z; envelopes completed_at 14:43:54-14:44:10Z; adjudicated 14:44:20Z), consistent with the development-smoke disclosure; all 12 card gates pass (1.08s); run_pr182_cas_axes.py --check and run_pr182_parity_registry.py --check both green; the card terminal is genuinely derived from adjudication bytes via the TERMINALS map with FAIL-withheld fallback, and hand-editing the adjudication would be caught by the byte-compare --check gate plus per-envelope status asserts; sibling_results_read=[] on all envelopes; the four axis sources are genuinely four distinct engine implementations (though structurally parallel translations of one design, per repo convention); registry module has no data path and the guard raises on any observed/extra argument. No P0: the CAS_4AXIS_PASS headline is factually supported because each axis internally asserts the same exact values as booleans; the P1s concern a falsely-documented verification layer (contract expected values enforced nowhere) and a misleading Lean computed-provenance surface feeding the cross-engine agreement gate — both should be fixed before the closure commit (all PR-182 artifacts except spec/contract/lean sources are still uncommitted).
